text:
maya: Hey team — customer (tenant: acme-inc) has 3x 401s in last hour. They claim their Okta tokens were valid and just rotated keys. Error from our gateway: "signature verification failed (kid mismatch)". Stack: auth-proxy v2.3.1.

maya: Quick paste of error lines:
```
2026-03-14T15:02:11Z auth-proxy ERROR verifyToken failed: kid not found in JWKS (kid="k_9f8a...")
2026-03-14T15:02:12Z auth-proxy ERROR fallback verify failed: signature invalid
```

maya: Customer says their IdP rotated keys ~15:55 UTC and our gateway still served the old jwks until 16:02 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260314-492 — Possible JWKS cache staleness (assigned: @alice)

kevin: @maya can you drop the raw token (redact) and the jwks url they're hitting? Need to reproduce locally. Also what's the cache ttl on edge?

maya: JWKS url: https://acme-okta.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
token header (redacted):
```
{"alg":"RS256","kid":"k_9f8a...","typ":"JWT"}
```

action: they use our hosted endpoint (us-east-1). Edge cache TTL currently 10m for jwks per runtime-config.

samir: A few things to check:
- If the token's `kid` is missing we fall back to trying all keys (slow). But here kid present and not found in cache.
- Could be CDN caching the JWKS with stale cache-control headers from their IdP.
- Also check clock skew: if token `iat`/`nbf` are off from our verifier our library may reject unless leeway set.

samir: Quick local repro steps I used:
```
# fetch jwks
curl -s -D - https://acme-okta.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json | head -n 40
# decode token header
echo 'eyJhbGciOiJS...' | cut -d'.' -f1 | base64 --decode
# verify signature with openssl (public key extracted)
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature sig.bin data.bin
```

alice: I pulled edge logs — we refetched jwks at 15:50, then again at 16:03. The cache TTL is 600s but we have a background refresh every 5m. Looks like customer rotated at 15:55 and CDN in front of their jwks served old payload until ~16:01.

kevin: So two vectors:
1) external JWKS delivery latency (their CDN)
2) our JWKS cache ttl + background refresh not aggressive enough to catch a rotation

maya: Also note one of the 401s has `iat` 2026-03-14T15:56:23Z while our gateway clock shows 15:49:30Z -> ~7m ahead. That's clock skew in customer's token issuer vs our servers.

samir: Right — our JWT verifier currently uses leeway of 60s for `exp/nbf/iat`. For heavy SSO integrations we should allow configurable leeway per-tenant or at least 10m for known IdPs. But increasing leeway has security implications (longer window).

alice: Short-term mitigation options:
- Force a JWKS refetch on signature failure when kid not found (try-to-refetch once, then fail). This avoids waiting for TTL expiry.
- Add extra diagnostics to logs: include token `kid`, jwks fetch timestamp, cache age, and raw jwks ETag/Cache-Control headers.
- Allow per-tenant verifier leeway override.

kevin: Can we implement the 'refetch-on-kid-miss' today as a patch? That seems low-risk.

samir: I can push a small change in auth-proxy: on verify if kid not found -> synchronous JWKS refetch and retry verification once. I'll add metrics to count these events. Target PR in next 3 hours.

maya: Customer update — they can tolerate 30s downtime. I'll ask them to rotate again at a scheduled time when we can watch.

jordan: FYI customer says their Okta uses aggressive CDN cache TTL=300 and sometimes origin is slow during rotations. We'll ask them to set short cache TTL or purge CDN on rotation.

kevin: Also add a temporary support playbook: steps to run when customer reports immediate signature errors: 1) check jwks endpoint headers, 2) request IdP purge, 3) request token reissue.

alice: Patch merged to staging: `auth-proxy: add-refetch-on-kid-miss` (deploying now). Also increased JWKS log verbosity for 1h window. :shipit:

samir: One more edge case — tokens signed with `kid=null` (common when symmetric or single-key setups). Make sure we handle missing kid gracefully and consider trying all keys with a short circuit on signature match.

maya: Verified with customer after patch — they retried and the requests succeeded at 16:12 UTC. They also rotated again and it was handled gracefully. Customer happy for now.

kevin: Action items:
- samir: production hotfix for refetch-on-kid-miss + metrics (in prod by EOD)
- alice: add cache-age and jwks-headers to error logs + runbook
- product/doc: create KB for customers on JWKS rotations and recommended cache-control

alice: Closing INC-20260314-492 after monitoring 1h with no regressions. Thanks all. :tada:

maya: :raised_hands: good job everyone
